criteria.scale_component: Body surface area affected by plaque-type psoriasis

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: 4.1 Inclusion criteria, criterion 4: "Moderate to severe psoriasis as defined at Randomization by:" "• PASI score of 12 or greater, and" "• IGA mod 2011 score of 3 or greater (based on a scale of 0 – 4), and" "• Body Surface Area (BSA) affected by plaque-type psoriasis of 10% or greater." -- The source explicitly calls the eligibility level moderate to severe and defines three conjunctive thresholds at randomization.

prohibited_concomitant: Treatments listed in Table 5-1 that could confound efficacy of the investigational drug are not allowed during the study for any indication; for psoriasis, use of a prohibited treatment during the study requires stopping that treatment to continue in the study.
permitted_concomitant: After Screening, psoriasis concomitant medication in all body regions is restricted to bland emollients and other non-medicated interventions.
Mild to moderate potency topical corticosteroids may be used on the face, scalp, and anogenital area during Screening only, and must stop at least the day before randomization.
Inhaled corticosteroids with only a topical effect, such as for asthma, are acceptable co-medication.
Antihistamines and corticosteroids in the eye, nose, or ear are unrestricted.

During Treatment Epoch II only, mild to moderate topical corticosteroids and other topical treatments are allowed if started after the Week 12 visit, used for no more than 14 consecutive calendar days, and for a non-psoriasis indication away from psoriasis-affected areas.
value.population_note: This protocol's Table 5-1 gives washout periods before randomization; those washouts are not treated here as blanket on-study prohibitions. The protocol separately states the on-study restriction and exceptions above. Background therapy is not characterized as monotherapy or standardized background topical treatment.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 5.5.8 Prohibited medication; Table 5-1 and footnotes: "Use of any treatments displayed in Table 5-1 that could confound the efficacy of the" "investigational drug is NOT allowed during the study for any indication." "use of concomitant medication for psoriasis in all body regions is restricted to bland emollients" "(not supplied by Novartis) and other non-medicated interventions." "Use of bland emollients must" "A mild to moderate potency topical corticosteroid (TCS) will be allowed for the treatment of" "the face, scalp, and anogenital area during the Screening Epoch." "These TCS should be stopped" "at least the day before the Randomization Visit." "Table 5-1 Prohibited medication by period/epoch (for any indication)" "Prohibited medicationa, b Washout period" "If a prohibited treatment of psoriasis was used during the study, the subject should discontinue use of the prohibited treatment if" "he/she wishes to continue in the study." "Exception: inhalative corticosteroids (CS) with only a topical effect (e.g., to treat" "asthma) are not considered" "systemic immunomodulating treatments" "and are therefore acceptable as co-medication." "There is no restriction on the use of anti-histamines and on the use of corticosteroids in the eye, nose or the ear" "Mild to moderate topical corticosteroids (TCS) are allowed only during the Screening Epoch if used only on the face, scalp" "and/or anogenital area and should be stopped the day before the Randomization visit." "Topical corticosteroids (mild to moderate) and other topical treatments will be allowed during Treatment Epoch II ONLY if (all" "must apply):" "- medication was started after the Week 12 visit was completed;" "- medication was used for 14 consecutive calendar days or less;" "- medication was used for an indication other than psoriasis and not on the area affected with psoriasis." "*** Inactivated virus vaccinations are allowed" -- The source's table heading identifies its before-randomization washout column; permitted screening and Treatment Epoch II exceptions are retained with their stated timing and conditions. The protocol does not describe a standardized background topical regimen or require emollient use.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 2.1 and 2.6.2 statistical testing strategy: "The level of significance will be set to 2.5% (one-sided, family-wise type-I-error)." "The co-primary endpoints are PASI 75 response and IGA 0 or 1 response at Week 12." "strategy and type-I-error will be set such that a family-wise type-I-error of α = 2.5% (one-sided)" "The graphical approach of (Bretz et al." "2009) for sequentially rejective testing" "procedures is used to illustrate the testing strategy:" "The testing sequence will continue to H3 at α (one-sided) only if both H1 and H2 have been" "Similarly, the testing sequence will continue to H4 at α (one-sided)" "corresponding alpha (α) will be passed to the next hypotheses corresponding H5." -- The SAP states one-sided family-wise type-I error at 2.5% (exactly 0.025) and describes a graphical sequentially rejective strategy. Co-primary endpoints are recorded separately; no fixed ordered sequence of the co-primary tests is asserted here.

value.source_inconsistency: The 8-week treatment-free Follow-up Epoch is only for early treatment discontinuations, after an EOTE visit approximately 4 weeks after the last dose. Table 6-1 places F4 and F8 after the Week 52 EOTEII column, while protocol text also describes F8 as 12 weeks after last study treatment; these are conditional follow-up timings, not an extension of completers' Week 52 study endpoint.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: 3.1 Study design; 3.2 Rationale; Table 6-1 Assessment schedule: "The study consists of 4 epochs: Screening (of at least 1 week and up to 4 weeks), Treatment" "Epoch I (of 12 weeks), Treatment Epoch II (of 40 weeks) and Follow-up." "The treatment-free" "phase of 8-week should only be completed in case of early discontinuations." "Screening (Screening to Randomization)" "The screening of at least 1 week and up to 4 weeks will be used to assess eligibility of the" "subjects and to taper-off prohibited medication(s)." "Treatment Epoch I (Randomization to Week 12 pre-dose)" "The Treatment Epoch I is defined as Randomization through Visit Week 12 (prior to Week 12" "dose)." "Treatment Epoch II (Week 12 post-dose to Week 52)" "The Treatment Epoch II is defined as Week 12 through Week 52." "For subjects who discontinue the study treatment prematurely for any reason before the End of" "the Treatment Epoch I, the End of Treatment Epoch I (EOTEI) Week 12 visit should be" "performed approximately four weeks after their last dose of study treatment (secukinumab or" "placebo)." "Thereafter, subjects should enter the treatment-free 8-week Follow-up Epoch." "Follow-up Epoch (8 weeks)" "reason will enter the treatment-free Follow-up Epoch to complete Visits F4 and F8 (as shown" "in Table 6-1)." "This 52-weeks, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, and placebo-controlled study is using" "The primary endpoint of this study is at Week 12." "last visit planned in the protocol (Visit Week 52 or Visit F8)." "Further, the subject should also return for the final Follow-up visits, F4 (8 weeks after last study" "treatment) and F8 (12 weeks after last study treatment) as shown in Table 6-1." "Table 6-1 lists assessments that are recorded in the clinical database." "Table 6-1 Assessment schedule" "Treatment Epoch I Treatment Epoch II FU U" "Week (Relative to 12a 13 14 15 16 20 24 28 32 36 40 44 48 52b" "≤-4 Ri 1 2 3 4 8 F4 F8b" "Randomization) EOTEI H H H H H H EOTEII" "Day R 8 15 22 29 57 85 92 99 106 113 141 169 197 225 253 281 309 337 365 393 421" -- Screening is stated as at least 1 and up to 4 weeks, so no fixed screening duration is entered. The 8-week Follow-up Epoch is conditional on early treatment discontinuation; whole-trial duration is therefore not calculated. The protocol itself contains the full per-visit Table 6-1. Follow-up visits are reported as F4 and F8 and are not converted to absolute weeks because their anchor depends on discontinuation timing.

published_results.source_excerpt: 14.1 Plaque Psoriasis, Trial PsO6 clinical outcomes, Table 5: "300 mg/2 mL Pre-filled Syringe and 300 mg/2 mL UnoReady Pen Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week trials (PsO6 and PsO7) enrolled 336 subjects at least 18 years of age with moderate to severe PsO who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy to evaluate the safety and efficacy of COSENTYX 300 mg subcutaneously administered with a single 300 mg/2 mL prefilled syringe (Trial PsO6, NCT02748863, 214 patients) or with a single 300 mg/2 mL UnoReady pen (Trial PsO7, NCT03589885, 122 patients) compared to two subcutaneous injections using a 150 mg/1 mL prefilled syringe." "The co-primary endpoints for both trials were the proportion of subjects who achieved a PASI 75 response and IGA mod 2011 ‘clear’ or ‘almost clear’ response with at least a two-grade reduction from baseline at Week 12." "Table 5: Clinical Outcomes at Week 12 in Adults With PsO in Trials PsO6 and PsO7 (Subcutaneous Treatment) Abbreviation: PFS, prefilled syringe." "Trial PsO6 Trial PsO7 COSENTYX 300 mg COSENTYX 300 mg 2 mL PFS (N = 72) % Two 1 mL PFS (N = 71) % Placebo (N = 71) % 2 mL Pen (N = 41) % Two 1 mL PFS (N = 41) % Placebo (N = 40) % IGA of clear or almost clear 76 69 1 76 68 8 PASI 75 response 89 82 2 95 83 10 PASI 90 response 67 70 2 76 62 5 14.2 Pediatric Plaque Psoriasis A 52-week, multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo and active-controlled trial (Trial PsO8; NCT02471144) enrolled 162 pediatric subjects 6 years of age and older, with severe plaque psoriasis (as defined by a PASI score ≥ 20, an IGA modified 2011 score of 4, and involving ≥ 10% of the BSA) who were candidates for systemic therapy." -- The label explicitly maps NCT02748863 to Trial PsO6. Table 5 separates Trial PsO6 from PsO7; only PsO6 columns are used. Values are printed percentages and N denominators, without responder counts. Timepoint is Week 12; the primary key endpoints match the label’s co-primary PASI 75 and IGA clear/almost-clear response at that time.
